title: observability: add token-level KV cache metrics, tracing spans, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Our recent incidents and ongoing cost-optimization work revealed a blind spot around per-request token economics and KV cache effectiveness. Operators need token-level cost and latency breakdowns correlated with KV-cache behavior to (1) triage latency regressions, (2) identify suboptimal cache hit patterns, and (3) tune alerts that map to business impact.

What this PR does: Adds token-level KV-cache metrics and tracing spans, a Grafana dashboard for cost/latency + KV insights, and tuned alerts for cache degradation and token-cost anomalies. Changes are low-risk instrumentation and dashboards, plus a small telemetry aggregation worker to emit pre-aggregated token buckets for efficient querying.

Summary of changes: Implemented server-side metrics emission for: token_count.total, token_count.gen, token_count.prompt, token_cost.estimated_usd, kv_cache.requests, kv_cache.hits, kv_cache.latency_ms (p95/p99), and a set of derived ratios (kv_hit_ratio, cost_per_token). Added tracing spans around KV cache lookup paths to attribute latency to cache vs model. Added a new telemetry worker (telemetry/token_aggregator) that rolls up per-request token-level events into minute buckets (configurable TTL) to reduce query pressure.

Dashboards: New Grafana dashboard "Token-level cost & KV cache" with panels for: cost/1000 tokens by model+route, token latency waterfall (prompt vs gen vs kv), KV hit heatmap by model+route, and correlated traces link. Dashboard uses existing templating (region, model, route).

Alert tuning: New alerts: KVCacheLowHitRatio (warning/critical), TokenCostSpike (adaptive threshold using historical baseline), KVLatencyDegradation (p99 > baseline + 50ms for 5m). Alerts include runbook links and recommended mitigation (fallback to smaller model, increase batching, clear bad cache keys). Thresholds are conservative; we'll iterate after 1 week of telemetry.

Performance and safety: Instrumentation paths guarded by feature flag observability.token_kv_metrics (off by default); telemetry worker defaults to sampling 1/10 for high-volume customers. Additional rate-limits added to ensure low CPU/IO cost. Unit and integration tests added for aggregation logic; e2e smoke on staging.

Rollout plan: 1) deploy to staging behind feature flag, 2) enable for canary orgs (internal + 3 customers) for 72 hours, 3) monitor telemetry and adjust alert thresholds, 4) flip feature flag account-wide. Rollback: disable feature flag and drain telemetry worker queue.

Related: Linear ENG-2187 (token observability roadmap), PM-405 (cost transparency), incident SUP-3422 (cache regression RCA).

review_conversation: Riley Park (reviewer): Can we ensure the aggregation worker won't cause increased egress? Suggest adding explicit TTL and size cap to buckets.
Ava Chen (author): Added TTL config and max_bucket_size config. Defaults chosen to be conservative (1MB per-minute per-shard).
Samir Patel (reviewer): Alerts look reasonable but TokenCostSpike should use a rolling baseline rather than fixed thresholds. Any plan?
Ava Chen (author): Alerts use Prometheus 'predict_linear' + percentile baseline for adaptive thresholds; updated rules and added runbook notes. Will monitor and iterate post-rollout.
Nina Gomez (reviewer): Small nit: tracing attribute names should be lowercase underscore to align with existing conventions.
Ava Chen (author): Renamed attributes to kv_cache.hit and kv_cache.key_hash; updated tests.
release_notes: Add token-level KV cache metrics, tracing spans, Grafana dashboard for token-level cost/latency and KV insights, and tuned alerts for KV hit ratio, KV latency, and token-cost spikes. Feature gated and rolled out gradually.
notes: Initial CI run flagged a linting style issue in token_metrics.go which was fixed in the second commit. Metrics and tracing are behind feature flag and sampling defaults to minimize overhead. Dashboard JSON is added but not auto-enabled in staging until feature flag is on.
